"Create a high-end, photorealistic survival horror game titled \"The Facility: Null\". 
Take as much time as your model limits allow—even if it takes up to 1 hour—to generate, build, script, and polish every single detail, visual asset, UI element, voice line, and mechanic to absolute perfection. Do not shorten or simplify anything.

0. CREATOR CREDIT @COMMENT_BODY@ TITLE SCREEN:
- Display the game title prominently on the main menu as: \"The Facility: Null\"
- Directly below the title, include the credit line: \"Created by °-° KING LOOK.S\" / \"Idee @COMMENT_BODY@ Konzept von °-° KING LOOK.S\" in a sleek, glowing metallic font.

1. LANGUAGE @COMMENT_BODY@ AUDIO SETTINGS:
- Language Options: The game settings, UI text, inventory, subtitles, and menus must be fully localized with a language switcher between German and English. 
- Menus @COMMENT_BODY@ Settings: Displayed in German by default (e.g., \"Einstellungen\", \"Grafik\", \"Multiplayer\", \"Steuerung\").
- Voice Acting @COMMENT_BODY@ Audio: All in-game dialogue, audio logs, radio calls, and character voices must remain in full, crystal-clear, professional English with precise 3D binaural spatial audio.

2. GRAPHICS @COMMENT_BODY@ VISUAL QUALITY:
- Photorealistic visual quality powered by high-resolution textures, volumetric atmospheric fog, ray-traced dynamic lighting, and realistic shadow effects.
- No global daytime lighting: the environment is dark, lit only by player flashlights, flickering emergency lights, and red alarm beacons.
- Extremely detailed indoor environments: abandoned underground medical complex, peeling wallpaper, cracked floor tiles, bloodstains, floating dust particles, and broken glass.

3. INTRO, GAME START @COMMENT_BODY@ STORY LORE:
- Game Intro: Starts with a cinematic cutscene. The player wakes up in a dark, locked security office. On a wooden desk sits a flickering lamp, a cassette recorder, and a blood-stained journal explaining the lore—an illegal genetic containment breach of a sound-sensitive host creature.
- Game Start: Players gather their starting items (a dying flashlight and a walkie-talkie) and must unlock the main security door to enter the facility.

4. OBJECTIVE @COMMENT_BODY@ GAME COMPLETION (WIN/LOSE CONDITIONS):
- Primary Objective: Navigate through 3 distinct sectors (Medical, Labs, Reactor) to collect 3 encrypted keycards, restore the main power generator, and activate the surface elevator.
- How the Game Ends (Victory): All surviving players must reach the surface elevator, call it down, defend the position for 60 seconds against the creature, and board the elevator to escape.
- Defeat Condition: If all players die or if the facility triggers its auto-detonation sequence before escaping, the game is lost.

5. SINGLEPLAYER MODE:
- Immersive, atmospheric solo experience with zero HUD on screen. 
- Health, stamina, and fear are displayed through in-game cues (heavy breathing, visible pulse, blurriness, blood splatters on screen).

6. MULTIPLAYER HUB @COMMENT_BODY@ MATCHMAKING:
Create a full-featured multiplayer system with three distinct options:
- A) Custom Private Lobby (Code System): The host creates a private lobby that generates a unique 4-character room code. Friends can enter this code in the menu to join the private session immediately.
- B) Quick Play (Public Matchmaking): One-click matchmaking that instantly pairs the player with random online players worldwide into an active 2-4 player lobby.
- C) Offline / Bot Match: Option to play multiplayer maps offline or fill empty slots with intelligent, cooperative AI bot teammates.

7. GAMEPLAY MECHANICS:
- 2 to 4 player co-op with proximity voice chat (creatures can hear players talking if they speak too loudly).
- Teamwork mechanics: sharing flashlight batteries, completing two-person puzzle interactions, and carrying/reviving downed teammates.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` ===PROMPT=== I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game using the existing project.
- Run and verify the game, then capture and inspect a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default UI with full German/English localization; voice acting and recordings remain in English.
- Dark underground medical facility with a cinematic security-office intro, lore, starting flashlight and walkie-talkie, and an unlockable security door.
- Three sectors, encrypted keycards, generator restoration, elevator escape defense, and win/lose conditions.
- Solo play with minimal HUD and in-world health, stamina, and fear cues; co-op lobby flows and 2–4-player mechanics.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobby behavior must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial menu, settings, lobby, intro, gameplay UI, and styling in `index.html` and `style.css`.
- Expanded `src/game.js` with Three.js setup, localization, procedural textures, facility construction, room props, and interactable objective setup.
- Added three keycard pickups, MED/LAB/elevator access interactions, generator gating, and elevator call interaction.
- Added objective UI, toast/audio helpers, journal and cassette lore interactions, and subtitles.
- Added monster and teammate models, player flashlight setup, ending UI logic, run reset, game start, and intro progression functions in `src/game.js`.
- Current changes are uncommitted.

### Active
- Finish `src/game.js`: movement, interaction handling, UI events, monster/bot updates, combat/damage, elevator-defense countdown, render loop, and remaining game flow.
- Validate and correct objective/keycard progression, collider behavior, generator, and elevator escape defense.
- Run the game, fix runtime/visual defects, and capture/inspect the requested JPEG.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the remaining `src/game.js` and implement player controls, interaction/event wiring, AI updates, countdown, and render loop.
2. Run syntax/runtime checks and test full progression; fix doors, keycards, colliders, generator, and elevator escape.
3. Launch the game, inspect it in a browser, fix defects, and capture/inspect a JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Active, incomplete game implementation; world setup, progression helpers, and some game systems are present.
- `index.html`: Menu, lobby, intro, gameplay HUD, pause, and ending markup.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive styling.
- `package.json`: Project metadata and dependencies.
- `capture.sh`: Existing screenshot capture wrapper.

## Important Context
- Facility room centers are `z=0,-17,-37,-60,-81`; gates are at `-6.45,-25.5,-49.3,-70.9`.
- Keycards are at `[-4,.9,-19]`, `[4,.95,-42]`, and `[-3,.95,-55]`; `collectKey(i)` advances `game.keys` to `i+1`, requiring cards in order.
- `buildWorld()` calls `makeMonster()`, `setupPlayerGear()`, `setupBots()`, and `updateObjectives()`; helper definitions now exist, but controls and game loop remain pending.
- `makeMonster()` sets `monster.userData.active=false`, while elevator call currently assigns `monster.active=true`; verify the AI’s activation state when implementing it.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game using the existing project.
- Run and verify the game, then capture and inspect a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default UI with full German/English localization; voice acting and recordings remain in English.
- Dark underground medical facility with a cinematic security-office intro, lore, starting flashlight and walkie-talkie, and an unlockable security door.
- Three sectors, encrypted keycards, generator restoration, elevator escape defense, and win/lose conditions.
- Solo play with minimal HUD and in-world health, stamina, and fear cues; co-op lobby flows and 2–4-player mechanics.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobby behavior must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added menu, settings, lobby, intro, gameplay UI, and styling in `index.html` and `style.css`.
- Built the Three.js facility, procedural textures, props, lore interactions, keycards, access gates, generator, elevator, monster, bots, HUD updates, and ending/reset helpers in `src/game.js`.
- Added player movement, collision checks, interaction handling, flashlight toggling, pause/settings/lobby event wiring, bot movement, monster pursuit/damage, elevator-defense countdown, and render loop in `src/game.js`.
- Changes remain uncommitted.

### Active
- Validate JavaScript syntax and runtime behavior; test the complete objective progression and fix any discovered issues.
- Run the game in a browser, inspect visuals, and capture/inspect a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Run syntax checks and launch the game; verify menu, intro, movement, interaction, pause, and lobby flows.
2. Test objective progression through journal, security door, three keycards, sector gates, generator, elevator call/defense, and escape; fix any bugs.
3. Inspect the running game in a browser, address visual/runtime defects, and capture/inspect the requested JPEG.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: World, progression, controls, AI, events, and render loop.
- `index.html`: Menu, lobby, intro, gameplay HUD, pause, and ending markup.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive styling.
- `package.json`: Project metadata and dependencies.
- `capture.sh`: Existing screenshot capture wrapper.

## Important Context
- Facility room centers are `z=0,-17,-37,-60,-81`; gates are at `-6.45,-25.5,-49.3,-70.9`.
- Keycards are at `[-4,.9,-19]`, `[4,.95,-42]`, and `[-3,.95,-55]`; `collectKey(i)` advances `game.keys` to `i+1`, requiring cards in order.
- Elevator defense lasts 60 seconds; the player must interact with the lift panel again once the countdown reaches zero.
- Monster activation is stored in `monster.userData.active`, but the elevator interaction currently sets `monster.active=true`; verify and correct this mismatch.
- `makeMonster()` adds the monster directly to `scene`; `buildWorld()` removes dynamic scene children before rebuilding.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game using the existing project.
- Validate gameplay, inspect the browser presentation, and capture and inspect a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default UI with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Dark underground medical facility with cinematic intro, lore, flashlight and walkie-talkie, and unlockable security door.
- Three sectors, keycards, generator restoration, elevator escape defense, and win/lose conditions.
- Solo play with minimal HUD and in-world health, stamina, and fear cues; co-op lobby flows and 2–4-player mechanics.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobby must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menu, settings, lobby, intro, gameplay UI, styling, procedural Three.js facility, story interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, pause/settings/lobby event wiring, and ending/reset helpers.
- `node --check src/game.js` passed.
- Started a local HTTP server on port 8000; `curl -sSI http://127.0.0.1:8000/` returned HTTP 200.
- Captured `/tmp/opencode/facility-menu.png` at 1280×720 and opened it for visual inspection.

### Active
- Fix and verify progression/gameplay defects, then test browser menu, intro, movement, interaction, pause, and lobby.
- Capture and inspect the requested JPEG (current capture is PNG, not JPEG).

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Fix the elevator monster activation mismatch (`monster.active=true` versus `monster.userData.active`), and inspect other objective/gate/progression defects.
2. Run the game in Chromium and verify menu, intro, movement, interactions, pause, and lobby.
3. Test progression through journal, security door, three keycards, sector gates, generator, elevator call/defense, and escape.
4. Capture and inspect a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: World construction, progression, controls, AI, event wiring, rendering.
- `index.html`: Menu, lobby, intro, HUD, pause, and ending markup.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive styling.
- `package.json`: Project metadata and dependencies.
- `capture.sh`: Existing screenshot capture wrapper.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Room centers use `z=0,-17,-37,-60,-81`; gates are at `-6.45,-25.5,-49.3,-70.9`.
- Keycards are at `[-4,.9,-19]`, `[4,.95,-42]`, and `[-3,.95,-55]`; `collectKey(i)` advances `game.keys` to `i+1`, requiring cards in order.
- Elevator defense lasts 60 seconds; interact with the lift panel again after countdown reaches zero.
- In `src/game.js`, elevator interaction sets `monster.active=true`, while `updateMonster()` checks `monster.userData.active`; correct the mismatch.
- `makeMonster()` adds the monster directly to `scene`; `buildWorld()` removes dynamic scene children before rebuilding.

## Objective
- Complete “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game using the existing project.
- Validate gameplay and browser presentation, and capture and inspect a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Dark underground medical facility with cinematic intro, lore, flashlight, walkie-talkie, and unlockable security door.
- Three sectors, keycards, generator restoration, elevator escape defense, and win/lose conditions.
- Solo play with minimal HUD and in-world health, stamina, and fear cues; local co-op lobby flows and 2–4-player mechanics.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menu, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural Three.js facility, story interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state event wiring.
- Fixed elevator monster activation mismatch in `src/game.js`: activation now uses `monster.userData.active=true`.
- `node --check src/game.js` passed after the fix.
- Local server on port 8000 responds HTTP 200.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/facility-menu.png` at 1280×720.

### Active
- Validate menu, intro, movement, interactions, pause, lobby, and full progression in Chromium.
- Investigate and fix any progression or gate issues found during playtesting.
- Capture and inspect the requested JPEG; current screenshot is PNG.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Run Chromium tests for menu, intro, movement, interaction, pause, and lobby.
2. Test the journal/security door, three keycards and sector gates, generator, elevator call/defense, and escape.
3. Capture a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: World construction, progression, controls, AI, and rendering.
- `index.html`: Menu, lobby, intro, HUD, pause, and ending markup.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive styling.
- `capture.sh`: Existing screenshot capture wrapper.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear untracked in `git status --short`.
- Room centers use `z=0,-17,-37,-60,-81`; gates are at `-6.45,-25.5,-49.3,-70.9`.
- Keycards are at `[-4,.9,-19]`, `[4,.95,-42]`, and `[-3,.95,-55]`; `collectKey(i)` advances `game.keys` to `i+1`.
- Elevator defense lasts 60 seconds; interact with the lift panel again after countdown reaches zero.
- `makeMonster()` adds the monster directly to `scene`; `buildWorld()` removes dynamic scene children before rebuilding.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game using the existing project.
- Validate gameplay and browser presentation, and capture and inspect a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Dark underground medical facility with cinematic intro, lore, flashlight, walkie-talkie, and unlockable security door.
- Three sectors, keycards, generator restoration, elevator escape defense, and win/lose conditions.
- Solo play with minimal HUD and in-world health, stamina, and fear cues; local co-op lobby flows and 2–4-player mechanics.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menu, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural Three.js facility, story interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state event wiring.
- Fixed elevator monster activation mismatch in `src/game.js`: activation uses `monster.userData.active=true`.
- Added an import map in `index.html` mapping `three` to `./vendor/three/three.module.js`; the previous “Failed to resolve module specifier "three"” error is resolved, and browser testing confirms menu-to-settings navigation works.
- `node --check src/game.js` passed; local server responds HTTP 200.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/facility-menu.png` at 1280×720.

### Active
- Validate intro, movement, interactions, pause, lobby, and full progression in Chromium.
- Investigate the remaining console 404 and screenshot capture timeouts.
- Capture and inspect the requested JPEG; `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` exists from an earlier attempt, but screenshot capture timed out waiting for fonts and it has not been validated as a successful capture.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser checks using Chromium with the import-map fix in place.
2. Identify the remaining 404 and resolve screenshot capture timeouts; avoid assuming `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` is valid.
3. Test the journal/security door, three keycards and sector gates, generator, elevator call/defense, and escape.
4. Capture and inspect a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: World construction, progression, controls, AI, and rendering.
- `index.html`: Menu, lobby, intro, HUD, pause, ending, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive styling.
- `capture.sh`: Existing screenshot capture wrapper.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear untracked in `git status --short`.
- Room centers use `z=0,-17,-37,-60,-81`; gates are at `-6.45,-25.5,-49.3,-70.9`.
- Keycards are at `[-4,.9,-19]`, `[4,.95,-42]`, and `[-3,.95,-55]`; `collectKey(i)` advances `game.keys` to `i+1`.
- Elevator defense lasts 60 seconds; interact with the lift panel again after countdown reaches zero.
- `makeMonster()` adds the monster directly to `scene`; `buildWorld()` removes dynamic scene children before rebuilding.
- Browser debug confirmed settings navigation now works; a console 404 remains. Screenshot attempts time out at Playwright’s “waiting for fonts to load...” step.

## Objective
- Complete “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game using the existing project.
- Validate gameplay and presentation, and capture and inspect a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Dark underground medical facility with cinematic intro, lore, flashlight, walkie-talkie, and unlockable security door.
- Three sectors, keycards, generator restoration, elevator escape defense, and win/lose conditions.
- Solo play with minimal HUD and in-world health, stamina, and fear cues; local co-op lobby flows and 2–4-player mechanics.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menu, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural Three.js facility, story interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state event wiring.
- Fixed elevator monster activation mismatch in `src/game.js`; activation uses `monster.userData.active=true`.
- Added an import map in `index.html` mapping `three` to `./vendor/three/three.module.js`; browser testing confirms menu/settings navigation works.
- `node --check src/game.js` passed; server responds HTTP 200.
- Browser smoke test passed menu, settings/language change, local lobby/bots, game launch, and pause/resume.
- Diagnostics found no page errors or failed resource responses; local fonts loaded. Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` at 1280×720.

### Active
- Validate intro, movement, interactions, journal/security door, keycards and sector gates, generator, elevator call/defense, and escape.
- Resolve inconsistent browser gameplay-test results: latest `/tmp/opencode/facility-gameplay.mjs` enters the intro and launches, but movement and interactions did not visibly progress; it also logged a 404. Earlier diagnostics showed no failed resources.
- Verify and fix the apparent objective/prompt mismatch: `buildWorld()` initially adds a MED-card objective interaction prompt while `game.storyDone` is false and the actual objective instructs reading the journal first.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/facility-gameplay.mjs` output and game input/pointer-lock state to make browser movement/interactions observable and reliable.
2. Check journal-first objective, prompt targeting, and MED-card progression; fix any mismatch found.
3. Validate progression through the elevator defense and both ending conditions, then rerun resource/error diagnostics and confirm the JPEG remains within the width limit.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: World construction, progression, controls, AI, and rendering.
- `index.html`: Menu, lobby, intro, HUD, pause, ending, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-gameplay.mjs`: Latest gameplay test; movement/interactions were inconclusive.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-test.mjs`: Earlier browser smoke test.
- `/tmp/opencode/diag.mjs`: Resource/font diagnostics and CDP JPEG capture.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg`: Captured and inspected 1280×720 JPEG.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear untracked in `git status --short`.
- Room centers use `z=0,-17,-37,-60,-81`; gates are at `-6.45,-25.5,-49.3,-70.9`.
- Keycards are at `[-4,.9,-19]`, `[4,.95,-42]`, and `[-3,.95,-55]`; `collectKey(i)` advances `game.keys` to `i+1`.
- Elevator defense lasts 60 seconds; interact with the lift panel again after countdown reaches zero.

- `showJournal()` sets `game.storyDone=true`; the security panel interaction at `[2.4,1.25,-5.7]` unlocks the first gate.
- The latest gameplay test reported `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found)`, while prior diagnostics recorded no failed responses.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game using the existing project.
- Validate gameplay and presentation, and capture and inspect a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Dark underground medical facility with cinematic intro, lore, flashlight, walkie-talkie, and unlockable security door.
- Three sectors, keycards, generator restoration, elevator escape defense, and win/lose conditions.
- Solo play with minimal HUD and in-world health, stamina, and fear cues; local co-op lobby flows and 2–4-player mechanics.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menu, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural Three.js facility, story interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state event wiring.
- Fixed elevator monster activation mismatch in `src/game.js`; activation uses `monster.userData.active=true`.
- Added an import map in `index.html` mapping `three` to `./vendor/three/three.module.js`; browser testing confirmed menu/settings navigation.
- Browser smoke test passed menu, settings/language change, local lobby/bots, game launch, and pause/resume.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` at 1280×720.
- Updated gameplay test navigation to use `waitUntil: 'commit'` and input keys to Playwright-compatible lowercase values; browser events reach `document`.

### Active
- Diagnose why gameplay inputs do not change player position or trigger interactions: keydown events are received and `keysDown` updates, but `player.pos` remains `[0,0,2.4]`, nearest interaction remains null, and journal/security/card objectives do not progress.
- Identify and resolve the browser-test 404; the console reports `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found)`, but the URL has not yet been captured.
- Continue validating journal/security door, keycard and sector gates, generator, elevator call/defense, and both ending conditions.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the game update loop and its runtime timing/state to determine why player movement remains stationary despite received key events.
2. Capture failed request URLs and resolve the 404.
3. Re-run interaction and progression tests, then validate remaining gates, generator, elevator defense, and endings.
4. Confirm the final JPEG remains within the 1280px width limit.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: World construction, progression, controls, AI, and rendering; currently includes temporary `window.__gameDebug`.
- `index.html`: Menu, lobby, intro, HUD, pause, ending, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-debug.mjs`: Gameplay diagnostic script.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-gameplay.mjs`: Earlier gameplay test script.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-test.mjs`: Earlier browser smoke test.
- `/tmp/opencode/diag.mjs`: Resource/font diagnostics and CDP JPEG capture.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg`: Captured and inspected 1280×720 JPEG.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear untracked in `git status --short`.
- `node --check src/game.js` passed earlier.
- The debug test confirms keydown events (`KeyS`, `KeyE`) fire on `BODY`, and `keysDown` contains `KeyS` while held; however, player position does not change.
- `update(dt)` handles movement from `keysDown`; `animate()` calls `update(dt)` only when `game.mode==='playing'&&!game.paused`.
- Initial player position is `[0,0,2.4]`, yaw is `0`; journal is near `[.15,1.1,4.38]`, and security panel near `[2.4,1.25,-5.7]`.
- Journal must be read before security can unlock; the MED card is in the following sector at `[-4,.9,-19]`.
- Room centers use `z=0,-17,-37,-60,-81`; gates are at `-6.45,-25.5,-49.3,-70.9`.
- Elevator defense lasts 60 seconds; interact with the lift panel again after countdown reaches zero.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game using the existing project.
- Validate gameplay and presentation, including a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Dark underground medical facility with cinematic intro, lore, flashlight, walkie-talkie, and unlockable security door.
- Three sectors, keycards, generator restoration, elevator escape defense, and win/lose conditions.
- Solo play with minimal HUD and in-world health, stamina, and fear cues; local co-op lobby flows and 2–4-player mechanics.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menu, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural Three.js facility, story interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state event wiring.
- Fixed elevator monster activation mismatch in `src/game.js`; activation uses `monster.userData.active=true`.
- Added `index.html` import map for `three` → `./vendor/three/three.module.js`; browser smoke test passed menu/settings/language, local lobby/bots, launch, and pause/resume.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` at 1280×720.
- Diagnosed gameplay input failure: the browser harness throttles `requestAnimationFrame` to zero ticks, so the game update loop never runs.
- Replaced the RAF-driven loop in `src/game.js` with a 60Hz `setInterval` loop; movement and interactions now progress in browser testing.
- Gameplay test confirmed the player reaches and interacts with nearby radio and journal after movement; objective updates to finding the MED card.

### Active
- Fix/validate gameplay test routing and interactions: current script’s movement sequence does not yet consistently reach the security panel or card.
- Capture exact URLs for remaining 404 resource errors and resolve if project-related.
- Validate security door, keycard and sector gates, generator, elevator call/defense, and both ending conditions.
- Remove temporary debug instrumentation/artifacts from `src/game.js` after testing.
- Reconfirm final JPEG width remains within 1280px.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Adjust browser test movement and interaction path from the spawn desk to the security panel and verify journal → door → MED card progression.
2. Capture the URLs for the 404 responses and identify whether they are missing project assets or browser-generated requests.
3. Exercise remaining progression, generator, elevator defense, and ending states; fix any issues.
4. Remove debug hooks, rerun syntax/browser checks, and verify the final 1280px JPEG.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: World, progression, controls, AI, rendering, and newly timer-driven update loop.
- `index.html`: Menus, lobby, intro, HUD, pause/ending screens, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Presentation and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-debug.mjs`: Gameplay diagnostic script; its debug-hook queries now fail because the hook was removed.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-gameplay2.mjs`: Browser gameplay test script.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-test.mjs`: Earlier browser smoke test.
- `/tmp/opencode/diag.mjs`: Resource/font diagnostics and CDP JPEG capture.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg`: Captured and inspected 1280×720 JPEG.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear untracked in `git status --short`.
- `node --check src/game.js` passed after switching to the timer-driven loop.
- Browser test output confirms player movement works after the loop change; interaction text transitioned from `Funkgerät aufnehmen` to `Blutiges Einsatzjournal lesen`, and toast showed `Funkgerät aufgenommen.`
- Initial player position `[0,0,2.4]`; journal is near `[.15,1.1,4.38]`; security panel near `[2.4,1.25,-5.7]`; MED card at `[-4,.9,-19]`.
- Journal must be read before security can unlock. Room centers use `z=0,-17,-37,-60,-81`; gates are at `-6.45,-25.5,-49.3,-70.9`.
- Elevator defense lasts 60 seconds; interact with the lift panel again after countdown reaches zero.
- Browser console still reported `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found)` twice; exact URLs have not been captured.

## Objective
- Complete “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game using the existing project.
- Validate gameplay and presentation, including a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Dark underground medical facility with cinematic intro, lore, flashlight, walkie-talkie, and unlockable security door.
- Three sectors, keycards, generator restoration, elevator escape defense, and win/lose conditions.
- Solo play with minimal HUD and in-world health, stamina, and fear cues; local co-op lobby flows and 2–4-player mechanics.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menu, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural Three.js facility, story interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state event wiring.
- Fixed elevator monster activation mismatch in `src/game.js`.
- Added `index.html` import map for `three` → `./vendor/three/three.module.js`; browser smoke test passed menu/settings/language, local lobby/bots, launch, and pause/resume.
- Replaced RAF updates in `src/game.js` with a 60Hz `setInterval` loop; movement and timer updates worked in browser testing.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` at 1280×720.
- `node --check src/game.js` passed after the update-loop change.
- Identified the two 404 errors as browser requests for `http://127.0.0.1:8000/favicon.ico`, not game assets.

### Active
- Diagnose progression movement and validate security door, keycard and sector gates, generator, elevator call/defense, and both ending conditions.
- Remove temporary debug instrumentation (`window.__facilityDebug`) from `src/game.js`, then rerun syntax and browser checks.
- Verify final JPEG dimensions remain at most 1280px.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Rerun `/tmp/opencode/facility-progress-test.mjs` and inspect `window.__facilityDebug()` positions, yaw, and nearest interaction to diagnose movement/routing.
2. Exercise progression gates, keycards, generator, elevator defense, and win/lose endings; fix issues found.
3. Remove the debug hook, rerun browser and syntax checks, and confirm the screenshot dimensions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: World, progression, controls, AI, rendering, timer-driven update loop, and temporary debug hook.
- `index.html`: Menus, lobby, intro, HUD, ending screens, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Presentation and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-progress-test.mjs`: Browser test for progression and HTTP/console errors.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-gameplay2.mjs`: Earlier gameplay test script.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg`: Previously captured 1280×720 screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear untracked in `git status --short`.
- A browser progression test previously read the journal and updated the objective, but the security panel and MED card were not reached; the latest test attempt timed out waiting for `[data-action="intro"]`.
- Latest diagnostic hook exposes `{pos, yaw, keys, mode, nearest}` via `window.__facilityDebug()`.
- Initial player position `[0,0,2.4]`; journal near `[.15,1.1,4.38]`; security panel near `[2.4,1.25,-5.7]`; MED card at `[-4,.9,-19]`.
- Journal must be read before the security door can unlock. Room centers use `z=0,-17,-37,-60,-81`; gates are at `-6.45,-25.5,-49.3,-70.9`.
- Elevator defense lasts 60 seconds; interact with the lift panel again after countdown reaches zero.
- Latest `node --check src/game.js` passed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game using the existing project.
- Validate gameplay and presentation, including a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Dark underground medical facility with cinematic intro, lore, flashlight, walkie-talkie, and unlockable security door.
- Three sectors, keycards, generator restoration, elevator escape defense, and win/lose conditions.
- Solo play with minimal HUD and in-world health, stamina, and fear cues; local co-op lobby flows and 2–4-player mechanics.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menu, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural Three.js facility, story interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state event wiring.
- Fixed elevator monster activation mismatch in `src/game.js`.
- Added an `index.html` import map for `three` → `./vendor/three/three.module.js`; browser smoke test passed menu/settings/language, local lobby/bots, launch, and pause/resume.
- Replaced RAF updates in `src/game.js` with a 60Hz `setInterval` loop; movement and timer updates worked.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` at 1280×720.
- `node --check src/game.js` passed before the latest objective/debug edits.
- Browser progression test successfully used debug positioning to complete journal, security unlock, all three keycards, sector gates, generator, elevator call/defense timer, and win ending.
- Fixed `updateObjectives()` objective selection so MED keycard and subsequent progression objectives map to the right phases.

### Active
- Fix and validate normal player movement around the opening desk; direct movement test remained blocked, ending near `[0.692,0,2.14]`.
- Remove the temporary `window.__facilityDebug` instrumentation from `src/game.js`, then rerun syntax and browser checks.
- Verify final JPEG dimensions remain at most 1280px.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Diagnose the opening movement collision and test journal/security interactions through normal movement.
2. Rerun `/tmp/opencode/facility-progression-check.mjs` after the objective update; it already demonstrated the full progression and win via debug positioning.
3. Remove the debug hook and rerun `node --check src/game.js` plus browser smoke/progression checks.
4. Confirm `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` dimensions are ≤1280px.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: World, progression, controls, AI, rendering, timer-driven update loop, and temporary debug hook.
- `index.html`: Menus, lobby, intro, HUD, ending screens, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Presentation and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-progression-check.mjs`: Browser test covering the full progression and win ending.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-progress-test.mjs`: Earlier browser progression/movement test.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg`: Previously captured 1280×720 screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear untracked in `git status --short`.
- `window.__facilityDebug()` currently exposes state and setters including `setPos` and `setHold`; it was added for progression testing and still needs removal.
- Browser progression test completed the win ending using direct debug positioning; ordinary movement around the opening desk remains unresolved.
- Observed HTTP/console 404s were favicon requests; the progression test filtered favicon HTTP errors but reported two generic console 404 messages.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game and validate gameplay and presentation, including a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Include the dark medical facility, intro, lore, equipment, progression, co-op lobby flows, and win/lose conditions.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menus, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural facility, interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state wiring.
- Confirmed normal keyboard movement changes player position; earlier movement tests failed to detect it because they lacked position visibility.
- Verified journal interaction advances the objective to finding the MED keycard.
- Confirmed `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` is a 1280×720 JPEG.

### Active
- Validate unlocking the opening security door through normal controls; the action has not yet been confirmed.
- Replace or update `/tmp/opencode/facility-progression-check.mjs`, which relies on debug methods not currently exposed.
- Rerun browser smoke/progression tests, inspect errors, and refresh the screenshot if needed.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Test reaching and activating the security panel with normal controls.
2. Update the progression script to use supported controls or provide appropriate test instrumentation, then verify progression and endings.
3. Recheck browser errors and screenshot dimensions; report the online multiplayer backend limitation.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Movement/collision, interactions, progression, AI, rendering; currently exposes a minimal `window.__facilityDebug()` with position, mode, pause state, held keys, and yaw.
- `index.html`: Menus, lobby, intro, HUD, ending screens, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Presentation and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-progression-check.mjs`: Existing test script; expects `window.__facilityDebug().setPos()` and other fields not provided by the current minimal debug function.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg`: Previously captured 1280×720 JPEG.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and appear untracked in `git status --short`.
- Current debug instrumentation was re-added in `src/game.js`; remove it after testing if not needed.
- Earlier browser runs noted 404s, including favicon requests.

## Objective
- Complete and validate “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game, including progression, endings, and a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Include the dark medical facility, intro, lore, equipment, progression, co-op lobby flows, and win/lose conditions.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menus, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural facility, interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state wiring.
- Confirmed journal interaction advances the objective to finding the MED keycard.
- Confirmed `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` is a 1280×720 JPEG.

### Active
- Validate unlocking the opening security door through normal controls; the player has not reached or activated its panel.
- Update `/tmp/opencode/facility-progression-check.mjs`, which expects unsupported debug methods (`setPos`, `setHold` and additional state fields).
- Re-run browser smoke/progression tests, inspect errors, and refresh the screenshot if needed.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Figure out a normal-controls route around the starting desk/obstacles to the security panel at `[2.4, 1.25, -5.7]`, then verify interaction after reading the journal.
2. Revise the progression test to use supported controls or add suitable test instrumentation; verify progression and endings.
3. Recheck browser errors and JPEG dimensions; report the online multiplayer backend limitation.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Movement/collision, interactions, progression, AI, rendering; currently exposes a minimal `window.__facilityDebug()` with position, mode, pause state, held keys, and yaw.
- `index.html`: Menus, lobby, intro, HUD, ending screens, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Presentation and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-progression-check.mjs`: Existing test script; its debug API assumptions do not match the game.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg`: Previously captured 1280×720 JPEG.
- `/tmp/opencode/panel-normal-controls.png`: Recent screenshot from a normal-controls attempt; the player did not reach the panel.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and appear untracked in `git status --short`.
- `window.__facilityDebug()` is currently minimal; no `setPos`, `setHold`, phase, keycard, power, or interaction-target fields.
- Normal movement works but was blocked by obstacles during the attempted route; the player ended around `[1.14, 0, -1.29]`, still near the journal.
- Browser navigation to `http://127.0.0.1:8000/` was intermittently slow; a longer navigation timeout succeeded. A prior console 404 was reported, likely a missing favicon.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and validate “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game, including progression, endings, and a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Include the dark medical facility, intro, lore, equipment, progression, co-op lobby flows, and win/lose conditions.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menus, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural facility, interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state wiring.
- Confirmed journal interaction advances the objective to finding the MED keycard.
- Confirmed `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` is a 1280×720 JPEG.
- Expanded `window.__facilityDebug()` in `src/game.js` to expose player position, mode, pause state, held keys, yaw, and collider geometry.
- Confirmed the old progression script assumes unsupported debug methods and state (`setPos`, `setHold`, and progression fields).

### Active
- Diagnose unreliable movement/access to the journal and security panel; recent browser testing showed movement from z=2.4 to about z=-0.7 after roughly two seconds of W input, without identifying a blocker.
- Replace `/tmp/opencode/facility-progression-check.mjs` with supported normal-controls testing or suitable instrumentation, then validate progression and endings.
- Recheck browser errors and refresh the screenshot if needed.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Investigate why movement slows/stops during forward travel and test reaching/activating the journal and security panel.
2. Update the progression test to use supported controls or add appropriate debug instrumentation; verify keycards, generator, elevator, and endings.
3. Recheck browser errors and JPEG dimensions; report the online multiplayer backend limitation.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Movement/collision, interactions, progression, AI, rendering, and debug API.
- `index.html`: Menus, lobby, intro, HUD, ending screens, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Presentation and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-progression-check.mjs`: Existing test script with unsupported debug API assumptions.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg`: Previously captured 1280×720 JPEG.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and appear untracked in `git status --short`.
- Security-panel interaction is at `[2.4, 1.25, -5.7]`; the opening in the initial room is centered at z `-6.5`.
- The security panel requires reading the journal first; the journal is at `[0.15, 1.1, 4.38]`.
- Medical, laboratory, and reactor keycards are at `[-4, 0.9, -19]`, `[4, 0.95, -42]`, and `[-3, 0.95, -55]`; the generator is at `[4, 1.2, -62]`.
- The elevator call requires power and starts a 60-second survival countdown.
- HTTP server was running at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`; one browser navigation waiting for full load timed out, while `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'` succeeded.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and validate “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game, including progression, endings, and a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Include the dark medical facility, intro, lore, equipment, progression, co-op lobby flows, and win/lose conditions.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menus, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural facility, interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state wiring.
- Confirmed journal interaction advances the objective to finding the MED keycard.
- Expanded `window.__facilityDebug()` with movement and progression state.
- Validated normal W movement and the journal-to-security-door interactions using Playwright; security gate unlocks and phase advances.
- Increased journal interaction radius from 2.2 to 2.5.
- Confirmed `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` is a 1280×720 JPEG.

### Active
- Validate keycard pickups, sector gates, generator, elevator countdown, and endings using obstacle-aware navigation.
- Investigate two browser console 404 errors from the latest Playwright run.
- Recheck browser errors and JPEG dimensions; refresh the screenshot if needed.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Continue `/tmp/opencode/facility-progression-check.mjs` from the security-door test; the latest run passed journal and security unlock.
2. Navigate around obstacles to test the MED, LAB, and REACTOR cards, access gates, generator, elevator countdown, and both endings; fix any issues found.
3. Identify the two 404 resources, then recheck browser errors and JPEG dimensions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Movement/collision, interactions, progression, AI, rendering, and expanded debug API.
- `index.html`: Menus, lobby, intro, HUD, ending screens, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Presentation and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-progression-check.mjs`: In-progress Playwright progression test; currently validates journal and security door.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg`: Previously captured 1280×720 JPEG.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and appear untracked in `git status --short`.
- HTTP server was running at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`; use `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'` because full-load navigation timed out.
- Starting position is `[0,0,2.4]`; the desk near `[0,.82,4.4]` blocks direct travel forward, and other furniture can obstruct routes.
- Journal is at `[0.15,1.1,4.38]`; security panel at `[2.4,1.25,-5.7]`, initial door centered at z `-6.45`.
- Medical, laboratory, and reactor keycards are at `[-4,0.9,-19]`, `[4,0.95,-42]`, and `[-3,0.95,-55]`; generator at `[4,1.2,-62]`.
- Elevator call requires power and starts a 60-second survival countdown; return to its panel after the timer to win.
- Latest test navigated to the security panel and confirmed phase 1; reported two console 404 errors.

- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Include the dark medical facility, intro, lore, equipment, progression, co-op lobby flows, and win/lose conditions.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menus, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural facility, interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state wiring.
- Confirmed journal interaction advances the objective and security-door interaction unlocks the gate and advances phase.
- Confirmed `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` is a 1280×720 JPEG.

- Diagnose the two browser console 404 errors and recheck browser errors and JPEG dimensions.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Rerun `/tmp/opencode/facility-full-check.mjs`; its BFS navigation grid origin was adjusted after it failed to find a path from the starting position, but that adjustment has not been tested.
2. Continue testing progression through the MED/LAB/REACTOR cards and access gates, generator, elevator countdown, and endings; fix any issues found.
3. Identify the two 404 resources, then recheck browser errors and JPEG dimensions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Movement/collision, interactions, progression, AI, rendering, and debug API.
- `index.html`: Menus, lobby, intro, HUD, ending screens, and Three.js imports.
- `style.css`: Presentation and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-full-check.mjs`: New Playwright navigation/progression test; currently unverified after grid adjustment.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-progression-check.mjs`: Earlier Playwright test passing journal and security unlock.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg`: Previously captured 1280×720 JPEG.

- Project files are uncommitted and appear untracked in `git status --short`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and validate “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game, including progression, endings, and a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Include the dark medical facility, intro, lore, equipment, progression, co-op lobby flows, and win/lose conditions.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menus, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural facility, interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state wiring.
- Confirmed journal interaction advances the objective; security panel interaction unlocks the gate and advances phase.
- Confirmed `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` is a 1280×720 JPEG.

### Active
- Validate keycard pickups, sector gates, generator, elevator countdown, and endings; the latest navigation test reached the security panel but failed during subsequent routing and timed out.
- Identify the two browser console 404 errors and recheck browser errors and JPEG dimensions.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Fix or replace the navigation routine in `/tmp/opencode/facility-full-check.mjs`; it currently incorrectly times out/misses routes after successfully unlocking the security gate.
2. Continue testing progression through the MED/LAB/REACTOR cards and access gates, generator, elevator countdown, and endings; fix any issues found.
3. Identify the two 404 resources, then recheck browser errors and JPEG dimensions.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-full-check.mjs`: Playwright navigation/progression test; currently unreliable after the security interaction.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-progression-check.mjs`: Earlier Playwright test passing journal and security unlock.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg`: Previously captured 1280×720 JPEG.
- `src/game.js`: Movement/collision, interactions, progression, AI, rendering, and debug API.
- `index.html`: Menus, lobby, intro, HUD, ending screens, and Three.js imports.
- `style.css`: Presentation and responsive styling.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and appear untracked in `git status --short`; recent edits were only to the temporary test script.
- HTTP server was available at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`; use `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'` because full-load navigation timed out.
- Starting position is `[0,0,2.4]`; desk near `[0,.82,4.4]` blocks direct travel forward, and furniture can obstruct routes.
- Journal is at `[0.15,1.1,4.38]`; security panel at `[2.4,1.25,-5.7]`, initial door centered at z `-6.45`.
- MED, LAB, and REACTOR keycards are at `[-4,0.9,-19]`, `[4,0.95,-42]`, and `[-3,0.95,-55]`; generator at `[4,1.2,-62]`.
- Elevator call requires power and starts a 60-second survival countdown; return to its panel after the timer to win.
- Latest test confirmed journal reading and security-door unlock. It reached approximately `[0.10,0,-10.65]` before the navigation attempt stalled/timed out.
- Two generic browser console errors remain: `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found)`.

## Objective
- Complete and validate “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game, including progression, endings, and a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Include the dark medical facility, intro, lore, equipment, progression, co-op lobby flows, and win/lose conditions.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menus, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural facility, interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state wiring.
- Confirmed journal interaction advances the objective and security-panel interaction unlocks the gate.
- Confirmed `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` is a 1280×720 JPEG.

### Active
- Validate progression through MED/LAB/REACTOR keycards and gates, generator, elevator countdown, and endings.
- Diagnose two browser console 404 errors; recheck browser errors.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser progression testing using `/tmp/opencode/facility-full-check.mjs`; it now gets through security and reaches approximately `[0.18,0,-10.14]`, but the browser/test times out before reaching the MED keycard.
2. Fix test navigation, then validate keycards, gates, generator, elevator countdown, and endings; address any gameplay issues found.
3. Identify the two 404 resources and recheck browser errors.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-full-check.mjs`: Playwright progression test and navigation helpers; latest version adds `goX`/`goZ` helpers but test has not completed.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-progression-check.mjs`: Earlier Playwright test passing journal and security unlock.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg`: Previously captured 1280×720 JPEG.
- `src/game.js`: Movement/collision, interactions, progression, AI, rendering, and debug API.
- `index.html`: Menus, lobby, intro, HUD, and ending screens.
- `style.css`: Presentation and responsive styling.

## Important Context
- Project files appear uncommitted and untracked in `git status --short`.
- Server responds at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`; use `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'` because full-load navigation timed out.
- Starting position is `[0,0,2.4]`; desk near `[0,.82,4.4]` blocks direct travel forward. Journal is at `[0.15,1.1,4.38]`; security panel at `[2.4,1.25,-5.7]`.
- MED, LAB, and REACTOR keycards are at `[-4,0.9,-19]`, `[4,0.95,-42]`, and `[-3,0.95,-55]`; generator at `[4,1.2,-62]`.
- Elevator call requires power and starts a 60-second survival countdown; return to its panel after the timer to win.
- Latest `/tmp/opencode/facility-full-check.mjs` run passed journal and security checks, reached the ward approach, then ended with `Target page, context or browser has been closed` after exceeding 180 seconds.
- Browser console previously reported two generic `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found)` errors. `index.html` references local fonts; assets include `assets/fonts/local-fonts.css` and font files, but no diagnosis is confirmed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and validate “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game, including progression, endings, and a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Include the dark medical facility, intro, lore, equipment, progression, co-op lobby flows, and win/lose conditions.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menus, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural facility, interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state wiring.
- Confirmed journal interaction advances the objective and security-panel interaction unlocks the gate in an earlier test.
- Confirmed `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` is a 1280×720 JPEG.

### Active
- Validate keycards, gates, generator, elevator countdown, and endings; the latest progression test could not navigate past the starting desk.
- Identify and resolve browser 404s; a latest page-load check reported one generic 404, while the progression check reported two.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Fix test navigation around the starting desk and security door; rerun progression testing from the MED keycard through both endings.
2. Identify the 404 resource(s) using the browser response URL/status logging, then rerun the browser error check.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-full-check2.mjs`: Latest progression test; its direct axis movement gets blocked by starting-area geometry.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-full-check.mjs`: Earlier grid-based navigation test; passed journal/security checks but timed out before the MED keycard.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-errors.mjs`: Browser HTTP/console error check.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-progression-check.mjs`: Earlier test passing journal and security unlock.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg`: Verified 1280×720 JPEG.
- `src/game.js`: Movement/collision, interactions, progression, AI, rendering, and debug API.
- `index.html`: Menus, lobby, intro, HUD, and ending screens.
- `style.css`: Presentation and responsive styling.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- Server responds at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`; browser navigation can time out even when the game loads, so use `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'` with a generous timeout.
- Starting position is `[0,0,2.4]`; desk near `[0,.82,4.4]` blocks direct travel forward. Journal is at `[0.15,1.1,4.38]`; security panel at `[2.4,1.25,-5.7]`.
- MED, LAB, and REACTOR keycards are at `[-4,0.9,-19]`, `[4,0.95,-42]`, and `[-3,0.95,-55]`; generator at `[4,1.2,-62]`.
- Elevator call requires power and starts a 60-second survival countdown; return to its panel after the timer to win.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-full-check2.mjs` used direct axis movement, which got blocked by colliders near the start; it did not reach the MED keycard or validate later progression.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-errors.mjs` reported `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found)` without identifying its URL.

## Objective
- Complete and validate “The Facility: Null” as a playable browser survival-horror game, including progression, endings, and a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- German-default interface with German/English localization; voice recordings remain in English.
- Include the dark medical facility, intro, lore, equipment, progression, co-op lobby flows, and win/lose conditions.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, local-first browser game built with Three.js.
- Local lobbies must not imply real online matchmaking; network multiplayer requires a hosted backend.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menus, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, procedural facility, interactions, progression objectives, AI, controls, and game-state wiring.
- Earlier browser test confirmed the journal advances the objective and the security-panel interaction unlocks the gate.
- Confirmed `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg` is a 1280×720 JPEG.
- Confirmed browser movement works in a focused test: W moved the player forward and D moved right.

### Active
- Validate keycards, gates, generator, elevator countdown, and endings; progression test still fails before reaching the MED keycard.
- Identify the URL responsible for the remaining browser 404.

### Blocked
- True network matchmaking and online multiplayer require a hosted backend.

## Next Move
1. Diagnose the progression test’s movement and route around the starting desk/security gate; resume testing from the MED keycard through both endings.
2. Capture and identify the 404 response URL, fix it if appropriate, and rerun browser error checks.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-full-check2.mjs`: Latest progression test; route/navigation is failing before the MED keycard.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-move-debug.mjs`: Focused keyboard-movement test; confirms W and D move the player.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-errors.mjs`: Browser HTTP/console error check; currently reports one generic 404.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-full-check.mjs`: Earlier grid-based navigation test; journal/security checks passed but it did not reach the MED keycard.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-final.jpg`: Verified 1280×720 JPEG.
- `src/game.js`: Movement/collision, interactions, progression, AI, rendering, and debug API.
- `index.html`: Menus, lobby, intro, HUD, and ending screens.
- `style.css`: Presentation and responsive styling.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- Server responds at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`; browser navigation can time out even when the game loads, so use `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'` with a generous timeout.
- Starting position is `[0,0,2.4]`; desk near `[0,.82,4.4]` blocks direct travel forward. Journal is at `[0.15,1.1,4.38]`; security panel at `[2.4,1.25,-5.7]`.
- MED, LAB, and REACTOR keycards are at `[-4,0.9,-19]`, `[4,0.95,-42]`, and `[-3,0.95,-55]`; generator at `[4,1.2,-62]`.
- Elevator call requires power and starts a 60-second survival countdown; return to its panel after the timer to win.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-full-check2.mjs` directly moves along axes but reports positions far short of targets; it has not validated progression beyond the starting area.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-errors.mjs` reports `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found)` without identifying its URL.
